one_liner: Zendesk has a broad REST API with OAuth 2.0 (auth code + PKCE); only a free 14-day trial gives working credentials, global OAuth for multi-tenant apps needs Zendesk approval; Zendesk now has its own official MCP server (via Zendesk Bridge, EAP).
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code (with PKCE) is the recommended method. API tokens (basic auth email/token:api_token) are being removed: unused tokens deactivate from July 28, 2026 and all stop by April 30, 2027. Multi-customer distribution requires global OAuth clients, which Zendesk must approve. Per-instance OAuth clients can be created in Admin Center.
access_notes: A free 14-day trial gives a working account and API. No permanent free tier is documented. Sponsored accounts are reserved for Marketplace partners. Individual developers are directed to their own instances or sandboxes.
blocker_notes: Only a 14-day trial is available without partnership. Multi-tenant distribution needs a global OAuth client approved by Zendesk. Per-instance OAuth clients are creatable in Admin Center.

evidence.quote: Zendesk Bridge provides a way to establish governed connections between the Zendesk MCP Server or Zendesk AI agents and external AI agents your organization uses
“Global” means Zendesk has approved the client for use across customer accounts.
If you plan on distributing an app, integration, or bot to multiple Zendesk customers, you must use global OAuth tokens to authenticate Zendesk API requests.
Starting July 28, 2026, unused tokens will automatically deactivate. By April 30, 2027, all API tokens will stop working.
You can try out the Zendesk platform with a free, 14-day trial account.
Customer developers or individual private app developers should use their own instances or sandboxes.
You'll find APIs for ticketing, help center, live chat, voice, sales CRM as well as some features that span capabilities
